chapters.title: Wizards, Recipes and Shared Resources
chapters.subtitle: Guided steps, ready-made setups and common building blocks

steps.text: This video covers three helpers that make a site easier to build and to use: the Wizard, which guides visitors through a form one step at a time; Recipes, which set up a site from a ready-made script; and the shared resources that other screens build on.

chapters.title: Why these three
chapters.subtitle: Long forms, repeated setups and repeated widgets

steps.text: A long form with dozens of boxes puts visitors off. Splitting it into steps, with progress shown, gets more of them to the end.
Setting up the same content types, roles and settings by hand on every new site is slow, and each site ends up slightly different.
Screens also need the same small widgets again and again, such as a date range menu or a phone box with flags, and they should look and behave the same everywhere.
The Wizard, Recipes and the shared resources answer one problem each, so you build once and reuse.

chapters.title: What each one is
chapters.subtitle: A wizard, a recipe and a shared resource

steps.text: A wizard asks a visitor for information one step at a time, remembers the answers between steps, and creates content items from them at the end.
A recipe is a ready-made setup that you run from the admin. It creates content types, settings, roles or sample content in one go.
The shared resources are the common scripts and styles that other CrestApps screens use, so a date range menu or a phone box behaves the same in every module.
You build a wizard in the admin and run recipes from the admin. The shared resources need nothing from you except to be turned on.

chapters.title: Prepare a wizard
chapters.subtitle: A content type with the Wizard part

steps.text: A wizard is a content type that has the Wizard part. Open Design, Content Definition, Content Types, and edit the type that will host the wizard. Here it is Workshop Registration.
Click Add Parts. Wizard is in the list. Click Add and Configure.
Contained content types are the kinds of step a wizard can have. Choose Visitor Details and Visit Preferences. Each step is an ordinary content type with its own boxes.

Requires an authenticated user is off, so anyone can take part. Tick it to require sign-in. Completion policy decides what happens to the answers at the end: create and publish them, create drafts, or do not keep them. Save.

chapters.title: Build the steps
chapters.subtitle: Add, fill in and order the steps

steps.text: Now create a Workshop Registration. Give it a title, such as Spring workshop.
Use Add step to add one card for each step, here Visitor Details and Visit Preferences. Each card holds that step's boxes, which can start with default values.
The order of the cards is the order of the steps, and you can drag a card to change it. Publish the item.
A link on your site sends visitors to the wizard. It opens on the first step, with a progress bar at the top that shows where they are.
The visitor fills in the first step and clicks Next. The progress bar marks it done, and the answers are kept.
On the second step, Previous goes back without losing anything, and Finish completes the wizard.
A confirmation page tells the visitor it is done.
With the completion policy on create and publish, each step's answers are now content items. Open Content, Content Items, and find the Visitor Details and Visit Preferences items.

chapters.title: Run a recipe
chapters.subtitle: A ready-made setup in one click

steps.text: Open Tools, Recipes. Recipes are grouped by feature. Each one has a name, tags, and a description of what it creates, so you know before you run it.
Type in the Search box to find a recipe by name or tag. Run starts a recipe and reports the result when it is done.
Recipes can also be pasted in. Open Tools, Deployments, JSON Import. The editor suggests the steps and their settings as you type, and marks mistakes before anything runs.
The date range menu offers presets such as Last 7 Days or This Month, and a custom range, in one dropdown. Report filters use it.
The phone box with a country flag picker is shared by the Phone Field and by screens that ask for a phone number.
Select-all checkboxes on admin lists, collapsible panels, date and time pickers and item selectors are shared in the same way.
Because they come from one place, every screen looks and behaves the same, and they are turned on once, together with the CrestApps features that use them.
Event or workshop registration that asks for details in a few short steps.
Customer onboarding, with one step for contact details and another for preferences.
A recipe that creates the same content types, roles and sample pages for every new site.
A recipe for a training or demo site, run again whenever you need a fresh copy.
Build a wizard once to guide visitors step by step, run a recipe to set a site up in one click, and let the shared resources keep every screen consistent. Thanks for watching.
